Lesson objective: A language model proposes an action; the program checks and executes it, then returns evidence.
Required components and relationships: Two balanced panels. Left: a blue speech card next to a person asking a question. Right: blue proposal card, an orange gate with a check mark, a teal weather instrument card, and a return teal evidence card feeding the blue model. Place the person outside the tool gate. Show no direct line from the blue model to the weather instrument bypassing the orange gate.
Text verbatim: "CHAT", "AGENT", "PROPOSE", "CHECK", "TOOL", "OBSERVE".

Lesson objective: The input context has finite capacity and must be selected deliberately.
Required components and relationships: A single large outlined open tray holds four clearly separated stacks: a small orange rule card, blue recent conversation cards, teal selected source cards, and a blank output reservation area. Do not imply that old cards magically remain available inside.

Lesson objective: Execution traces explain what happened, while evaluations judge whether the answer met a criterion.
Required components and relationships: Two balanced panels. Left: a nested execution timeline represented by one long blue parent bar with three indented orange/teal child bars and one marked failure spot, no numbers or scales. Right: a report page beside a rubric with one approved evidence row and one orange revision row; use source cards as evidence for the rubric. Keep the two panels connected by the same report icon.
